title: Why super() must be the first constructor statement
answer: A superclass constructor must run before the subclass can use the object as a fully initialized child, because inherited state is part of the same object. Java therefore requires an explicit `super(...)` or `this(...)` constructor invocation to occur first in a constructor. This prevents subclass code from operating on inherited state before superclass initialization. AeroTopo follows the rule with `super(id, tiles)` as the first statement in `Orthomosaic`.
